name: fclose
description: Closes a file opened with fopen. Returns 0 if the stream was closed successfully, or EOF if an error occurred.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file to close.

name: feof
description: Tests whether the end-of-file indicator on the stream was set by the last read operation. Returns a nonzero value if EOF has been reached, 0 otherwise.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file to check.

name: ferror
description: Tests whether an error occurred during a file I/O operation. Returns 0 if there is no error, or a nonzero value if there is one (the stream's error indicator remains set).

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to a file previously opened with fopen.

name: fgetc
description: Reads a single character from the stream. Returns the character read, or EOF if the end of the file is reached or a read error occurs.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file to read from.

name: fgets
description: Reads a line of text from a file into a buffer. Returns the string read, or a null pointer if end of file is reached or a read error occurs.

args.name: string
args.desc: Destination buffer for the string read.

args.name: maxchar
args.desc: Maximum number of characters to read.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file to read from.

name: fopen
description: Opens a file for buffered I/O and returns a FILE pointer, or NULL on failure. Access modes: r, w, a, r+, w+, a+ (the + modes require the file to exist); append t for text mode or b for binary mode.

args.name: filename
args.desc: Name (path) of the file to open.

args.name: access_mode
args.desc: Access mode and file type, e.g. "r", "w", "a", "rb+".

name: fprintf
description: Writes formatted output to a file. Returns the number of characters written, or a negative value if an error occurs.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the destination file.

args.name: format_string
args.desc: Format string written to the file.

args.name: args
args.desc: Optional arguments to print (one or more).

name: fputc
description: Writes a single character to the stream. Returns the character written on success, or EOF on failure.

args.name: c
args.desc: Character to write to the stream.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the destination file.

name: fread
signature: size_t fread(void *buffer, size_t size, size_t count, FILE *file_pointer);
description: Reads unformatted (raw) data from a stream into a buffer. Returns the number of items successfully read; if fewer than count, an error or EOF occurred (distinguish with feof or ferror).

args.name: buffer
args.desc: Destination location for the data read.

args.name: size
args.desc: Size of each item in bytes.

args.name: count
args.desc: Maximum number of items to read.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the input stream.

name: fscanf
description: Reads formatted input from a stream. Returns the number of fields successfully read (not counting ignored fields); if EOF is reached before the first conversion, the result indicates an error.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file to read from.

args.name: format_string
args.desc: Format characters that control how the input is parsed.

args.name: args
args.desc: Destination arguments (variable addresses), matching the format specifiers.

name: fseek
signature: int fseek(FILE *file_pointer, long offset, int origin);
description: Moves the file position to a new location. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on failure. origin values: SEEK_SET (0) start of file, SEEK_CUR (1) current position, SEEK_END (2) end of file.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file.

args.name: offset
args.desc: Offset in bytes from the origin.

args.name: origin
args.desc: Starting point: SEEK_SET (0), SEEK_CUR (1), or SEEK_END (2).

name: fwrite
signature: size_t fwrite( const void *buffer, size_t size, size_t count, FILE *file_pointer);
description: Writes unformatted (raw) data from a buffer to a stream. Returns the number of complete items (not bytes) successfully written.

args.name: buffer
args.desc: Data to write.

args.name: size
args.desc: Size of the buffer/item (per the documentation).

args.name: count
args.desc: Number of items to write.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the destination file.

name: rewind
description: Resets the file position to the beginning of the file. Returns no value.

args.name: file_pointer
args.desc: Pointer to the file to reposition.

name: sprintf
description: Writes formatted output to a string. Returns the number of characters written, or a negative value on error. The destination buffer must be large enough; if the result exceeds its capacity, the script may behave unpredictably.

args.name: string_buffer
args.desc: Destination string buffer.

args.name: format_string
args.desc: Format characters.

args.name: args
args.desc: Optional arguments to print.

name: sscanf
signature: int sscanf(const char *buffer, const char *format_string, args);
description: Reads formatted input from a string. Returns the number of fields successfully read (not counting ignored fields).

args.name: buffer
args.desc: Source string to parse.

args.name: format_string
args.desc: Format characters.

args.name: args
args.desc: Destination arguments (variable addresses).

name: chdir
description: Changes the current working directory to the given path. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

args.name: path
args.desc: Path of the target directory.

name: chdrive
description: Switches to a different drive (Windows only). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

args.name: drive
args.desc: Drive number: 1 = A, 2 = B, etc.

name: getcwd
description: Retrieves the name of the current working directory into a buffer. According to the documentation, returns zero on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: path
args.desc: Destination buffer for the current directory path.

args.name: numchars
args.desc: Maximum number of characters to retrieve.

name: getdrive
description: Returns the current drive as a number (1 = A, 2 = B, etc.; Windows only). Returns -1 on failure.

name: ftell
description: Returns the current file position of the stream. On error, returns -1 and sets errno. Commonly used with fseek(SEEK_END) to determine the file length.

args.name: stream
args.desc: FILE pointer identifying the stream.

name: mkdir
description: Creates a new directory at the given path. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

args.name: path
args.desc: Path and name of the directory to create.

name: remove
description: Deletes the specified file. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (errno is set to the error code).

args.name: path
args.desc: Full path of the file to delete.

name: rmdir
description: Deletes the specified directory. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (errno is set to the error code).

args.name: path
args.desc: Full path of the directory to delete.

name: abs
description: Returns the absolute value of an integer.

args.name: n
args.desc: Integer value whose absolute value is returned.

name: cos
description: Computes the cosine of an angle in radians. Returns the result as a double. Note: 180 degrees = PI radians.

args.name: x
args.desc: Angle in radians.

name: floor
description: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to x (rounds down). Returns a double.

args.name: x
args.desc: Value to round down.

name: rand
description: Generates a pseudo-random integer between 0 and 32767. Call srand first to seed the random number generator.

name: sin
description: Computes the sine of an angle in radians. Returns the result as a double.

args.name: x
args.desc: Angle in radians.

name: sqrt
description: Computes the square root of x. If x is negative, the result is indefinite (documentation sample output: -1.#IND00).

args.name: x
args.desc: Value whose square root is computed.

name: srand
description: Seeds the pseudo-random number generator; must be called before rand(), typically as srand(time(NULL)).

args.name: seedTime
args.desc: Seed value for the random number generator.

name: time
description: Returns the current system time as the number of seconds since January 1, 1970 UTC; the same value is also stored in timeptr unless it is NULL.

args.name: timeptr
args.desc: Pointer to a time_t variable that receives the result; if NULL, the value is not stored.

name: ctime
description: Converts calendar time to a human-readable local time string. Note: on Linux this function is not thread-safe; use ctime_r.

args.name: calTime
args.desc: Pointer to the calendar time value to convert.

name: localtime
description: Converts calendar time to local time and returns a pointer to a struct tm. Note: on Linux it is not thread-safe; use localtime_r.

args.name: calTime
args.desc: Pointer to the calendar time value to convert.

name: gmtime
description: Converts calendar time to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and returns a pointer to a struct tm. Note: on Linux it is not thread-safe; use gmtime_r.

args.name: calTime
args.desc: Pointer to the calendar time value to convert.

name: asctime
description: Converts a time in a struct tm to a human-readable string. Note: on Linux it is not thread-safe; use asctime_r.

args.name: tmTime
args.desc: Pointer to the struct tm to convert.

name: strftime
signature: size_t *strftime(char *string, size_t maxlen, const char *format, const struct tm *timestruct);
description: Converts a time to a formatted string and writes it to a memory area. Returns the number of characters written (excluding the null terminator), or 0 on failure. Note: on Linux it is not thread-safe; use strftime_r.

args.name: string
args.desc: Destination buffer for the resulting string.

args.name: maxlen
args.desc: Maximum buffer capacity, including the null terminator.

args.name: format
args.desc: Format string (platform-dependent).

args.name: timestruct
args.desc: Pointer to a struct tm from gmtime() or localtime().

name: getenv
description: Retrieves the value of an environment variable. Returns NULL if the variable does not exist.

args.name: varname
args.desc: Name of the environment variable.

name: putenv
description: Adds a new definition to the environment table. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

args.name: envstring
args.desc: String in the format "varname=value".

name: system
description: Executes an operating system command by passing the string to the OS. Returns 0 on success, or -1 on failure (errno: ENOENT, ENOEXEC, ENOMEM, E2BIG).

args.name: string
args.desc: Command passed to the operating system.
